comment: Shared shell session return-target corpus. `path` is the request path and query the portal server validates before restoring it after login (control/lib/symmetry_control_web/portal_session.ex, PortalSession.return_to/1); the client rebuilds the same location from an absolute URL (frontend/src/app/application.ts, safeReturnTo) and must agree case by case. The enumerated accept/reject cases are pinned on both sides, so every path or query rule change on either side must add a corpus case; only the cases listed here are compared. `return_to` is the accepted target echoed back, or null when the target is refused: the server then falls back to /portal and the client to /portal/attention. This file is deliberately outside the wire-fixture manifest (`fixtures/manifest.json`) and its `pnpm contracts:check` validation: it describes shell URL acceptance, not a wire payload, and only `control/test/symmetry_control_web/portal_session_test.exs` and `frontend/src/app/application.test.ts` consume it. Three raw-string asymmetries stay out of the corpus because a single `path` string cannot express both sides: a bare trailing `#` (the parsed URL hash is empty, so the client accepts and emits the location without it, while the server receives fragment "" and refuses), an empty `?` query (the client's URL parser normalizes it away and the location is accepted, while the server refuses the empty query), and absolute, protocol-relative or backslash host forms (`https://host/portal/...`, `//host/portal/...`, `\\host\portal`) that the client's URL parser resolves to an authority or a same-origin path while the server refuses any raw string carrying a scheme or host — or, for the backslash form, matching no shell path. The empty-query and bare-fragment forms are pinned per side instead, in the reject list of the ExUnit test `login accepts only explicit internal shell return paths` (control/test/symmetry_control_web/portal_session_test.exs) and in frontend/src/app/application.test.ts.
